operations.name: Saw Cut Blank
operations.setup_note: Locate round bar against the length stop and cut individual blanks for the provisional X-axis machining route. Release stock procurement only after material and geometry clarifications are closed.

operations.name: CNC Turn – First End
operations.setup_note: Grip the opposite raw-stock end in soft jaws, using steady support where needed, and face the exposed arm end. Run a consolidated canned profile on the accessible first-side boss and shoulder regions, retaining the stock required for the arms and non-axisymmetric datum-A protrusion.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Second End
operations.setup_note: Reverse the blank into bored soft jaws locating on the first-operation cylindrical surfaces and an axial stop. Face the opposite arm end to the overall length and complete the remaining boss, shoulder and blend regions without removing the retained prismatic-feature stock.

operations.name: VMC – Datum A, Arms and Slots
operations.setup_note: Locate on the turned shoulders in a supported, mechanically indexable fixture that retains one clamping while presenting the datum-A flanks, arm surfaces and through-slot direction. Rough the datum surfaces first and all thin-section features before finishing; then finish and pick up A, finish the arms, establish B with the right slot, and finish the left slot from A–B.

operations.name: Production Deburr and Clean
operations.setup_note: Support the machined component without marking datum A and rapidly remove machining burrs, including both slot exits. Break sharp edges within the drawing's 0.5 mm maximum, then remove chips and cutting-fluid residue.

operations.name: Local Bond-Zone Surface Preparation
operations.setup_note: Present the fully machined parts to a qualified vendor for localized abrasive preparation of F06, with surrounding finished surfaces protected. This provisional process must be confirmed against the applicable bond-preparation specification before release.

operations.name: Batch Phosphate Coat
operations.setup_note: Process the 100-piece order on the in-house bulk phosphate line, splitting it into rated barrel loads as necessary and protecting the finished geometry from handling damage. Clean and verify a water-break-free surface before applying PS-119.0 phosphate, followed by the specification-required rinsing and drying.

operations.name: Final Shop-Floor Quality Gate
operations.setup_note: Seat the finished part in a dedicated datum-A nest and use slot-boundary gauges with the appropriate MMC datum-B simulation to verify the slot pattern. Perform sampled shop-floor checks of arm dimensions, parallelism, shoulders and coating condition using dedicated gauges and SPC records rather than 100% CMM layout.

clarifications.question: Which material grade is required to meet the specified minimum yield strength of 690 MPa?
What hardness is required for the supplied material?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use certified, machinable stock below approximately 45 HRC that already satisfies the specified mechanical properties; add no manufacturing heat treatment.

clarifications.question: Is X the common rotational axis of the central outer profile and both external Ø42 shoulders?
clarifications.suggested_default: Provisionally use X for the two turning setups, preserving stock for all non-axisymmetric features; do not release turning until confirmed.

clarifications.question: Can you provide the released 3D model defining the central external contour?
Is the 23.6–23.9 mm long axis of each slot actually along Z, given that the confirmed arm width along Z is only 21.62–22.38 mm?
Does the formed-area thickness-variation note require this component to be manufactured by forming rather than machining from solid stock?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat the note as applicable only where formed areas exist, not as a mandatory blank-manufacturing instruction.

clarifications.question: Can you provide the controlling PS-119.0 phosphate process specification?
clarifications.suggested_default: Provisionally assume full-surface phosphate with dimensional buildup accommodated before coating; release requires confirmation of the actual process requirements.

clarifications.question: What surface-preparation specification applies to the F06 bond zone on BP00B369210?
clarifications.suggested_default: Localized abrasive preparation before phosphate, with no bond-incompatible oil or sealer on F06; confirm because the extracted PS-135.22 reference names BP00B369211.

assumptions.text: This is a provisional hybrid route, not a production-released process. The extracted geometry does not establish an unambiguous rotational model, and the slot long dimension conflicts with the confirmed arm width; the blocking clarifications must be closed before machining.

The provisional stock envelope uses 200 mm along X and a 70.92 mm maximum circular cross-section, giving a 75 mm diameter by 208 mm blank. The reported 7.39 mm and 22.38 mm envelope values are not treated as the complete central-body envelope.

Standard round stock is selected for the 100-piece order because neither a forged blank nor mandatory directional grain flow is specified. The formed-area note alone does not establish a forming requirement; mandatory forming would invalidate this stock selection and require a revised route.

The customer's supplied interpretation of F07 is accepted: its 2X Ø42 callout identifies the same external shoulders as F04, not internal bores. Turning therefore physically produces both feature records, and no hole-making or bore-finishing route is required.

ALM-ROUTE-001 and ALM-TURN-001 are applied as two consolidated lathe setups. Separate diameter-specific sub-operation records represent nonoverlapping portions of each G71/G70 profile, not repeated full-depth roughing cycles: F03 represents accessible axial bands, and F04/F07 represent the corresponding first-side or second-side shoulder.

The R2.5 shoulder blends require dedicated groove/form cutting after adjacent diameters are finished. They are retained within their respective lathe setups rather than assigned additional workholdings.

ALM-VMC-001 is applied through one retained-clamp VMC fixture with mechanical indexing, subject to confirmed tool access. VMC sub-operations 1–8 are roughing and 9–16 are finishing; each repeated face or side-milling record addresses a distinct flank or opposing surface. Straddle milling may replace paired side cuts only where cutter and fixture clearance permit it.

The VMC establishes rough datum surfaces first, roughs all thin-section features before final finishing, then finishes and picks up datum A before finishing dependent features. The right slot establishes B before the left slot's final boundary is machined; finish milling uses climb cutting.

The turning template's center drilling is omitted because steady support avoids creating unshown center holes. Internal boring and threading are omitted because no such features remain after resolving F07; general edge breaking is consolidated at the deburr gate, and parting is unnecessary because individual blanks are sawn and both ends are faced.

The milling template's pocketing, center drilling, drilling, reaming, tapping, countersinking and counterboring are omitted because no corresponding features are identified. The elongated holes are produced directly by slot milling; their sizes and positions must be resolved before cutting.

F06 is provisionally produced by localized abrasive preparation at an outside vendor because blasting capability is not listed in-house. Its preparation method and position relative to phosphating remain subject to the applicable bonding specification.

ALM-BENCH-001 is applied by using the in-house bulk phosphate line rather than outsourcing coating. Coating masking and unmasking are provisionally omitted because no precision bore, thread or explicitly uncoated mating surface is identified; specification-defined exclusions would require those steps.

The surface-treatment template's cure/bake is provisionally omitted because phosphate is not a thermoset coating and the supplied information does not establish a hydrogen-embrittlement relief requirement. Material certification and PS-119.0 must resolve this before coating; if relief is required, add qualified outside baking within the specified time window, including the four-hour limit where applicable.

All dimensional cutting, radiusing and deburring precede phosphate. General edge breaks are provisionally 0.3–0.5 mm to satisfy the coating-edge rule without exceeding the drawing maximum; coated dimensions must accommodate the actual specified buildup.

No manufacturing heat treatment or post-hardening finishing is added because none is specified. Material is provisionally classified as medium-machinability stock below approximately 45 HRC; ALM-FEAS-003 requires outside heat treatment, transport and subsequent hard finishing only if the confirmed material requirements introduce hardening.

ALM-BENCH-002 and ALM-INSP-001/002 are applied through rapid production deburr/clean gates and sampled dedicated-gauge inspection, not prolonged hand finishing or 100% CMM layout. The common final quality gate satisfies both machining templates and the coating-inspection step; functional or destructive testing is omitted because none is specified.
